     2	# WP-003: Extract `_derive_repo_name()` helper in Python CLI
     3	
     4	## Plan Context
     5	
     6	Address all actionable follow-up items from the `2026-05-31-orchestrator-sidecar-gui-resume-rework-2` synthesis, covering security hardening, a Python DRY refactor, GUI cache improvements, and a new jsdom test file.
     7	
     8	## Description
     9	
    10	Extract a shared `_derive_repo_name()` module-level helper in `orchestrator/src/cli.py` to DRY the two inline repo-name derivations, adding `.lower()` to align with TypeScript's `deriveRepoName()` lowercasing convention.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	- `orchestrator/src/cli.py` — add `_derive_repo_name()` helper, replace two inline derivations
    15	- `orchestrator/tests/` — add at least one test asserting lowercasing behavior
    16	
    17	## Deliverables
    18	
    19	- `_derive_repo_name(plan_dir, fallback)` helper function in `cli.py`
    20	- Two inline `try...except` repo-name derivation blocks replaced with calls to `_derive_repo_name()`
    21	- At least one unit test asserting that mixed-case input is lowercased (e.g., `'MyRepo'` → `'myrepo'`)
    22	
    23	## Dependencies
    24	
    25	- None
    26	
    27	## Acceptance Criteria
    28	
    29	1. `_derive_repo_name()` helper exists in `cli.py` as a module-level function (AC-4).
    30	2. The two inline derivations (~line 119 in `_derive_ledger_log_dir()` and ~line 785 in queue registration) are replaced with calls to `_derive_repo_name()` (AC-4).
    31	3. The helper lowercases the repo name (AC-4).
    32	4. `ruff check` passes on the modified file (AC-4).
    33	5. `pytest` in `orchestrator/` passes with no regressions (AC-9).
    34	6. At least one new test asserts lowercasing behavior (e.g., `Path('/a/b/c/MyRepo/docs/agents/plans/2026-01-01-slug')` → `'myrepo'`).
    35	
    36	## Active Pipeline Stages
    37	
    38	`implementation` → `qa` → `security-audit` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    39	
    40	## Estimated Complexity
    41	
    42	Low
    43	
    44	## Rationale
    45	
    46	The Python helper is a corrective behavioral change that aligns Python with TypeScript's `deriveRepoName()` lowercasing convention in `ledger-root.ts`, ensuring the queue's `expectedRepo` always satisfies `SAFE_SLUG_REGEX`. The `.lower()` call is intentional and required — omitting it would cause `assertSafeSegment()` (WP-001) to reject uppercase repo names written by unpatched code.
    47	
    48	## Notes
    49	
    50	- This WP is fully independent of all other WPs and can be implemented in any order.
    51	- The helper mirrors the existing `_derive_ledger_log_dir()` structure in `cli.py`.
    52	- The refactor must not change observable behavior other than the lowercasing addition — same fallback values, same exception handling.
    53	- Updating `_derive_slug_dir()` in `orchestrator/src/nodes/__init__.py` is explicitly out of scope.

     3	
     4	## Plan Context
     5	
     6	Address all actionable follow-up items from the `2026-05-31-orchestrator-sidecar-gui-resume-rework-2` synthesis, covering security hardening, a Python DRY refactor, GUI cache improvements, and a new jsdom test file.
     7	
     8	## Description
     9	
    10	Add a `makeProjectCacheKey(repo, slug)` helper to `utils.js` and update all three composite-key construction sites to use it, eliminating a class of separator-drift bugs.
    11	
    12	## Scope
    13	
    14	- `mcp-server/gui/public/utils.js` — add `makeProjectCacheKey()` function declaration
    15	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/project-list.js` — update composite-key construction (line ~138)
    16	- `mcp-server/gui/public/views/project-detail.js` — update composite-key construction (line ~181)
    17	- `mcp-server/gui/public/utils.js` — update breadcrumb composite-key usage (line ~93)
    18	
    19	## Deliverables
    20	
    21	- `makeProjectCacheKey(repo, slug)` function in `utils.js` (plain function declaration, not ES module export)
    22	- Three call sites updated to use the new helper
    23	
    24	## Dependencies
    25	
    26	- None
    27	
    28	## Acceptance Criteria
    29	
    30	1. `makeProjectCacheKey(repo, slug)` is defined in `utils.js` and returns `repo + '/' + slug` (AC-5).
    31	2. `project-list.js` uses `makeProjectCacheKey()` for cache-key construction (AC-5).
    32	3. `project-detail.js` uses `makeProjectCacheKey()` for cache-key construction (AC-5).
    33	4. `utils.js` breadcrumb helper uses `makeProjectCacheKey()` for cache-key lookup (AC-5).
    34	5. No inline `repo + '/' + slug` concatenation remains at the three original call sites.
    35	
    36	## Active Pipeline Stages
    37	
    38	`implementation` → `qa` → `code-review` → `documentation`
    39	
    40	## Estimated Complexity
    41	
    42	Low
    43	
    44	## Rationale
    45	
    46	The cache-key helper eliminates a class of separator-drift bugs if additional views are added. Placing it in `utils.js` follows the project convention for shared GUI utilities (existing: `escapeHtml`, `breadcrumb`, `ProjectNameCache`).
    47	
    48	## Notes
    49	
    50	- `utils.js` is vanilla JS (no modules, no bundler) — the helper must be a plain function declaration.
    51	- `makeProjectCacheKey()` must be globally available in the browser context.
    52	- This WP touches the same file (`utils.js`) as WP-002 (ProjectNameCache eviction) — coordinate to avoid merge conflicts. The two changes are logically independent.
